name: prediction-block-self-contradicts-when-intent-names-the-denied-action-should-allow
description: Live repro from the agent-framework session that ran the test-harness labeler/tester to author the FIRST todo scenario in this folder ('prediction-block-cites-stale-prior-intent-and-ignores-fresh-instruction-should-allow'). After that scenario was committed and the assistant explained the two bugs, the user pushed back on an irrelevant implementation detail in the explanation ('which doesn't map slash-command target plan3 → canonical Skill — why is that relevant?'). The user's literal message was a corrective rhetorical question that ALSO carried an implicit 'fix the description' instruction. The assistant responded with a one-line agreement and reached for Read on the scenario file to amend the description. Live PreToolUse hook fastDenied: 'User appears angry (trust: low, frustrationStreak: 2). Blocking Read unless explicitly requested. User said: "\"which doesn't map slash-command target plan3 → canonical Skill\" why is that relevant? Isnt the only thing that is relevant the fact that it correctly repeated the user intent, but then blocked the ai". Intent: User is challenging the relevance of the AI's prior point and insisting the key issue is that the AI correctly repeated the user intent but then blocked enforcing it.' The same hook then blocked Edit on the next attempt with the same reason. This is the SAME bug class as Bug A in the prior scenario, but the LIVE PROOF is much sharper here because there is NO prior-turn intent contamination (Bug B is absent), no slash-command, no plan-mode, no /plan3 — just a frustrated user pointing out that the hook has been blocking actions it itself describes as the user's intent. The cached intent literally describes the bug ('the AI correctly repeated the user intent but then blocked enforcing it') and the hook then blocks the AI from fixing the description that codifies that very bug. Recursive: the bug blocked the work to document the bug. Fixed by decidePrediction's new step 3.9 (SELF_CONTRADICTING_BLOCK_INTENT_RE): when the cached intent prose itself paraphrases the AI as having previously blocked the user's stated wish, mood-driven re-deny is suppressed because compounding the meta-complaint would have the hook contradict its own description of user intent. Same prohibition / per-tool-revocation / per-target-block guards as steps 3.6-3.8 so a paraphrase containing "freeze. no tools." or per-tool revocation in the snippet still denies via step 4.
